method: Both the retiring SwissJob scraper and the new Core adapter were replayed offline against this SAME sealed capture, so the parity below is byte-level.

transport_contract.why_not_the_public_listing: /stellen builds its offers with JavaScript and answers 200 with zero offer links — the defect that killed this source (VD.4b).
transport_contract.required_header: Referer: https://www.gastrojob.ch/stellen (the frontend sends it and the endpoint expects it)
transport_contract.own_ads_only: /stellen/stelleninserat/<digits>; partner ads under /stellen/externe-partner/ are not harvested

preserved_verdicts: a fragment without the advertisement counter is a visible failure, not an empty page
an unreadable counter is a visible failure — including one of thousands of digits, which makes int() raise (the scraper's own r2/H4 fix, reproduced here with a test that bites)
own offer links of which none parses is a visible failure, decided BEFORE the page-range verdict
beyond the last page the counter covers is a legitimate end of pagination
a partner-only page inside the range is a legitimate empty page — the rehabilitation path
anything else inside the range is a visible failure, even mid-sweep after good pages
identity_rules_preserved: the stored URL is REBUILT from the canonical path: a tracking query, a port or a different case do not create a second row
the host is validated, so a protocol-relative, userinfo or cross-host href cannot move the stored URL
the company comes only from the listing, even when the detail microdata knows it: it is part of the legacy identity and only the listing is stable run to run
notes: No credential exists for this source and none was created.
The artifact carries no personal data: only byte counts, hashes and aggregate counters.
Today's capture has zero anonymised ads; the scraper's own probes measured between ~3 % and ~13 %, and those stay 'Unknown' by design.
Core does not reproduce the cursor early-stop: it sweeps the five declared pages, which is 55 requests per run at the portal's own two-second pace.
